claim: Manual vibe-checking fails at scale: informal evaluation plateaus into a whack-a-mole loop, and Hamel's framework prescribes three levels (programmatic unit-test asserts, human+model eval, A/B testing) with model-based judges validated against human labels.
quote: limited visibility into the AI system's effectiveness across tasks beyond vibe checks ... You must continue doing periodic exercises to monitor the model and human agreement

claim: G-Eval uses chain-of-thought-generated evaluation steps plus a form-filling, log-probability-weighted scoring paradigm and achieved the highest Spearman correlation with human judgments (0.514) on SummEval, but does not directly eliminate verbosity or self-preference bias.
quote: G-Eval achieved the highest Spearman correlation with human judgments (0.514), outperforming all baselines ... G-Eval doesn't directly eliminate narcissistic bias

claim: Self-preference bias is formally measurable as the gap in an evaluator favoring itself; on Chatbot Arena (33k dialogues, 8 LLM judges) GPT-4 showed the highest self-preference bias score of ~0.520 (favorable recall 0.945 vs unfavorable 0.425).
quote: GPT-4 exhibits the highest bias ... a self-preference bias score of approximately 0.520 ... recall rates of 0.945 (favorable cases) and 0.425 (unfavorable cases)

claim: No judge is uniformly reliable: a RAND study found consistency broke down on formatting changes and paraphrasing, JudgeBiasBench found frontier models exceeding 50% error on advanced bias tests, and 80% human-agreement and 50% bias-error findings coexist rather than conflict.
quote: No judge evaluated by the RAND Corporation's research team was uniformly reliable across benchmarks ... Frontier models exceeded 50% error rates on advanced bias tests ... The 80% agreement finding and the 50% error rate on bias benchmarks are not in conflict

claim: LLM-evaluators carry documented position bias (claude-v1 biased toward first position 70% of the time), verbosity bias (claude-v1 and gpt-3.5 preferred the longer response >90% of the time), and self-enhancement (gpt-4 +10%, claude-v1 +25% self win-rate), with poor sensitivity on factual-consistency tasks, so they are not reliable enough to systematically replace human judgment.
quote: Both claude-v1 and gpt-3.5 preferred the longer response more than 90% of the time ... Gpt-4 favored itself with a 10% higher win rate while claude-v1 favored itself with a 25% higher win rate ... they're not reliable enough to systematically replace human judgments

claim: Direct scoring by LLMs is misaligned with humans in a way calibration cannot fix; reframing evaluation as pairwise preference ranking (PAIRS) produces rankings inherently more aligned with human judgment, which is why pairwise comparison is favored for subjective evals.
quote: A systematic analysis of LLMs used as direct scorers revealed a misalignment between LLM and human evaluators, which cannot be effectively mitigated by applying calibration techniques

claim: 2026 practitioner guidance enumerates five named LLM-judge biases (position, verbosity, self-preference, format, calibration drift) and treats 'never use the same model as judge and candidate' as a cardinal rule since self-preference adds 10-25% uniform bias.
quote: position, verbosity, self-preference, format, and calibration drift ... never use the same model as judge and candidate, as self-preference adds 10 to 25 percent uniform bias
